title: Dedicated Capacity — Pool Operations & Autoscale Control UI (prototype & review)
creator: Ava Rios
description:
Goal: Create a clear, actionable UI in Redwood Console for Dedicated GPU pool operations that surfaces pool health, makes autoscaling and burst controls discoverable and safe, and provides fast recovery/rollout actions for platform operators.

Problem: Current Dedicated capacity pages are fragmented: health signals are buried, autoscaling controls are split between infra config and a separate admin panel, and there is limited in-UI guidance for safe burst or manual scaling operations. Customers operating latency-sensitive workloads need an operator-centric dashboard that reduces time-to-diagnose and makes temporary capacity changes low-risk.

Scope: Design the pool-level overview (single pane summarizing health across nodes), a right-hand inspector for configuration and controls (autoscale policy, burst budget, maintenance mode), and a compact rollback/rollout action flow (canary %, fallback model pool mapping). Include responsive layouts, keyboard accessibility for key controls, and compact mobile view for on-call workflows. Prototype will include 3 states: healthy, degraded (high queue/evictions), and emergency (node failures + capacity exhausted).

Assumptions & constraints:
- UI must read signals exposed by ENG endpoints (see ENG-2881) so data availability will drive refresh cadence.
- Autoscale changes are rate-limited server-side; UI should warn and debounce repeated requests.
- Burst capacity is a limited budget per pool; design must prevent accidental depletion.
- RBAC: only users with pool-owner or infra-admin can change scaling policies; others see read-only views.

Proposed screens and primary interactions (high level):
1) Pool Overview card (top): pool name, region, total GPUs, active nodes, current allocation %, short summary health pill (green/yellow/red), last updated timestamp. Quick actions: Open Inspector, Start Manual Scale, Enter Maintenance.
2) Health timeline (middle): 24h sparkline for GPU utilization, request queue length, avg P50/P95 latency per token, eviction rate. Hover reveals exact values and links to Grafana.
3) Node grid (bottom-left): compact cards for each host/GPU with status, model variants pinned, mem usage, last heartbeat, recent errors. Click host -> host detail flyout with logs link.
4) Inspector / Controls pane (right): Tabs for Configuration | Autoscale | Burst & Limits | Rollouts. Autoscale tab shows current policy (min/max/growth window), recommended policy (from Optimize), and an edit flow that validates inputs and simulates projected capacity curve. Burst & Limits shows remaining burst budget and cooldown window, with a protected 'Apply burst' modal requiring reason and optional dry-run.
5) Rollouts: Surface canary controls for model variants bound to the pool, allow scheduling of canary% and automatic rollback triggers (latency/regression thresholds). Include an audit trail link.

Design decisions under consideration:
- Inline recommendations: show Optimize suggestions directly in Autoscale tab vs. separate CTA. Trade-off: convenience vs. potential confusion about authoritative policy. Recommendation: show recommendation as non-authoritative banner with preview button.
- Burst as a modal + cooldown vs. inline toggle: choose modal to make budget/justification explicit and to capture audit metadata.
- Health pill semantics: prefer multi-dimensional summary (traffic/latency/evictions) with mouseover breakdown rather than a single metric to avoid masking regressions.

Telemetry & observability hooks to include in UI: GPU_utilization_pct, request_queue_length, avg_token_latency_ms_p50, avg_token_latency_ms_p95, eviction_rate_pct, node_heartbeat_missing, autoscale_events, burst_consumed_units, rollout_regressions. Provide direct linkouts to Grafana and the rollout debug trace.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Edit autoscale with unsafe min/max could trigger oscillation. Mitigation: provide simulated projection, show recent scaling events, and require cooldown window >= 60s in UI validation.
- Risk: Burst misuse could drain committed capacity. Mitigation: show remaining budget prominently, require reason and limit on simultaneous pool-level bursts.
- Risk: RBAC confusion could lead to accidental UI actions. Mitigation: disabled controls show hover tooltip explaining permission and link to admin docs.

Deliverables for the ticket:
- Figma prototype (3 pool states) with interactive autoscale edit flow and burst modal.
- Design spec doc with accessibility annotations, error states, and copy for modals/toasts.
- Hand-off checklist for ENG (API endpoints required, expected payloads, validation rules, rate-limits).
- Usability notes from stakeholder review and next steps for dev QA.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with Pool Overview, Health timeline, Node grid, and Inspector controls is complete and linked
Autoscale edit flow allows editing min/max/growth-window, validates inputs, and shows a simulated capacity curve
Burst modal requires justification, displays remaining budget, and enforces cooldown visual guidance
Rollout canary controls allow scheduling, set rollback thresholds, and surface recent rollout regressions
All interactive controls respect RBAC: admin vs read-only users are shown appropriate affordances
Performance metrics (utilization, queue, p50/p95, evictions) are visible and link to Grafana dashboards
Design spec includes keyboard-accessible equivalents and ARIA notes for primary controls
Handoff includes a minimal API contract and list of telemetry metrics needed for display and alerts
comments: 2026-02-20 - Kickoff: Met with PM (Nora Patel) and ENG (Diego Torres) to align on data availability and safe autopolicy edits. Agreed to surface Optimize suggestions but keep final control with users.
2026-02-25 - Prototype v0.1 uploaded to Figma. Focused on card layout and health timeline. Initial feedback: PM requests clearer separation between recommended policy and applied policy.

2026-03-02 - Stakeholder review: Infrastructure team requested that burst modal include an optional TTL and ability to tag bursts as 'incident' to bypass some checks. Security asked for an audit note saved to event log.
2026-03-05 - Accessibility audit (mini): Labeling for graph tooltips needed; color-only cues not sufficient for health state. Will add icons and textual statuses.
2026-03-10 - Engineering sync: ENG-2881 will expose autoscale_events, burst_budget_remaining, and node_heartbeat_missing. We adjusted timeline to wait for these metrics before final polish.

2026-03-12 - Design review with CEO/CTO watch: Emphasized low-risk defaults (no auto-approve for burst) and a clear rollback path. Next: polish copy, add simulated capacity chart, finalize handoff materials.
